text:
Given below are two statements : one is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R.

Assertion A : Fluorine forms one oxoacid.

Reason R : Fluorine has smallest size amongst all halogens and is highly electronegative.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are correct but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is correct but R is not correct.
A is not correct but R is correct.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Fluorine forms only one oxoacid, $\mathrm{HOF}$ (hypofluorous acid, also called fluoric(I) acid). Chlorine, bromine and iodine form series such as $\mathrm{HOX}$, $\mathrm{HOXO}$, $\mathrm{HOXO}{}_{2}$ and $\mathrm{HOXO}{}_{3}$.

Fluorine is the smallest and the most electronegative halogen, so it cannot show positive oxidation states or expand its octet; this is why it forms only one oxoacid. Assertion A and Reason R are both correct, and R is the correct explanation of A.

$\mathrm{OF}{}_{2}$ and $\mathrm{O}{}_{2}\mathrm{F}{}_{2}$ are oxygen fluorides (oxides), not oxoacids, so they do not affect Assertion A.

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th June Evening Shift

text:
Arrange the following coordination compounds in the increasing order of magnetic moments. (Atomic numbers : Mn = 25; Fe = 26)

A. [FeF$_{6}$]$^{3-}$

B. [$Fe(CN)_{6}$]$^{3-}$

C. [MnCl$_{6}$]$^{3-} ($high spin)

D. [$Mn(CN)_{6}$]$^{3-}$

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Spin-only moment $μ=\sqrt{n(n+2)}$ BM rises with the number of unpaired electrons $n$.

A. $[\mathrm{FeF}{}_{6}]{}^{3-}$: $\mathrm{Fe}{}^{3+}$, $3d^{5}$; weak-field $\mathrm{F}{}^{-}$ gives high spin $t_{2g}^{3}e_{g}^{2}$, $n=5$, $μ=5.92$ BM.

B. $[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN}){}_{6}]{}^{3-}$: $\mathrm{Fe}{}^{3+}$, $3d^{5}$; strong-field $\mathrm{CN}{}^{-}$ gives low spin $t_{2g}^{5}e_{g}^{0}$, $n=1$, $μ=1.73$ BM.

C. $[\mathrm{MnCl}{}_{6}]{}^{3-}$ (high spin): $\mathrm{Mn}{}^{3+}$, $3d^{4}$, $t_{2g}^{3}e_{g}^{1}$, $n=4$, $μ=4.90$ BM.

D. $[\mathrm{Mn}(\mathrm{CN}){}_{6}]{}^{3-}$: $\mathrm{Mn}{}^{3+}$, $3d^{4}$; strong-field $\mathrm{CN}{}^{-}$ puts all four electrons in $t_{2g}$, $t_{2g}^{4}e_{g}^{0}$, which still leaves 2 unpaired electrons, $μ=2.83$ BM.

The increasing order of magnetic moment is $\text{B}<\text{D}<\text{C}<\text{A}$.

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th June Evening Shift

text:
Match List I with List II.

  
    
    List-I 
(Anion)
    
    List-II 
(gas evolved on reaction with dil.H${}_{2}$SO${}_{4}$)
  

  
    (A)
    CO${}_{3}^{2-}$
    I.
    Colourless gas which turns lead acetate paper black.
  
  
    (B)
    S${}^{2-}$
    II.
    Colourless gas which turns acidified potassium dichromate solution green.
  
  
    (C)
    SO${}_{3}^{2-}$
    III.
    Brown fumes which turns acidified KI solution containing starch blue.
  
  
    (D)
    NO${}_{2}^{-}$
    IV.
    Colourless gas evolved with brisk effervescence, which turns lime water milky.
  

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
With dilute $\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{SO}{}_{4}$ each anion gives a characteristic gas.

$\mathrm{CO}{}_{3}{}^{2-}$: $\mathrm{CO}{}_{3}{}^{2-}+2\mathrm{H}{}^{+}\longrightarrow \mathrm{CO}{}_{2}+\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}$; $\mathrm{CO}{}_{2}$ comes off with brisk effervescence and turns lime water milky by forming $\mathrm{CaCO}{}_{3}$: IV.

$\mathrm{S}{}^{2-}$: $\mathrm{S}{}^{2-}+2\mathrm{H}{}^{+}\longrightarrow \mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{S}$; $\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{S}$ turns lead acetate paper black by forming $\mathrm{PbS}$: I.

$\mathrm{SO}{}_{3}{}^{2-}$: $\mathrm{SO}{}_{3}{}^{2-}+2\mathrm{H}{}^{+}\longrightarrow \mathrm{SO}{}_{2}+\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}$; $\mathrm{SO}{}_{2}$ reduces acidified dichromate to green $\mathrm{Cr}{}^{3+}$: II.

$\mathrm{NO}{}_{2}{}^{-}$: the nitrous acid formed decomposes, $3~\mathrm{HNO}{}_{2}\longrightarrow \mathrm{HNO}{}_{3}+2\mathrm{NO}+\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}$, and NO is oxidised by air to brown $\mathrm{NO}{}_{2}$ ($2~\mathrm{NO}+\mathrm{O}{}_{2}\longrightarrow 2\mathrm{NO}{}_{2}$). These brown fumes oxidise iodide in acidified KI to $\mathrm{I}{}_{2}$, which turns starch blue: III.

So A-IV, B-I, C-II, D-III.

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th June Evening Shift

text:
Consider the following set of quantum numbers.

  
    
    n
    l
    m${}_{l}$
  

  
    A.
    3
    3
    $-$3
  
  
    B.
    3
    2
    $-$2
  
  
    C.
    2
    1
    +1
  
  
    D.
    2
    2
    +2
  

The number of correct sets of quantum numbers is $__________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For A,

Given n = 3 and l = 3

but we know maximum value of l = n $-$ 1.

$\therefore$ l can't be equal to n.

So, Set A of quantum numbers is not possible.

For B,

Given n = 3, l = 2, m = $-$ 2

Here, l = 2 which follow the rule l = n $-$ 1.

And we know possible value of m is $-$ l to + l.

here possible value of m = $-$2 to +2

$\therefore$ This Set B is valid set of quantum numbers.

For C,

Given n = 2, l = 1, m = +1

Here l = 1 which follows the rule l = n $-$ 1.

For l = 1 possible value of m = $-$1 to +1

Here m = +1. So value of m is valid.

$\therefore$ Set C is valid set of quantum numbers.

For D,

Given n = 2, l = 2, m = +2

l = 2 does not follow the rule l = n $-$ 1 rule.

$\therefore$ Set D is not valid set of quantum numbers.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th June Evening Shift

text: A solution containing 2.5 $\times$ $10^{-3} kg$ of a solute dissolved in 75 $\times$ $10^{-3} kg$ of water boils at 373.535 K. The molar mass of the solute is $____________ g$ mol$^{-1}$. [nearest integer] (Given : $K_{b}(H_{2}O) = 0.52 K kg$ mol$^{-1}$ and boiling point of water = 373.15 K)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$W_{\text{solute}}=2.5\times 10^{-3}\mathrm{kg}$

$\begin{array}{l} \mathrm{W}_{\text{solvent}}=75\times 10^{-3}\mathrm{kg} \\  \\ \Delta \mathrm{T}_{\mathrm{b}}=373.535-373.15 \\  \\ =0.385\mathrm{K} \\  \\ \mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{b}}(\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O})=0.52\mathrm{K}\mathrm{kg}\mathrm{mol}^{-1} \\  \\ \Delta \mathrm{T}_{\mathrm{b}}=\dfrac{\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{b}}\times 10^{3}\times \mathrm{W}_{\text{solute}}}{\mathrm{M}_{\text{solute}}\times \mathrm{W}_{\text{solvent}}} \\  \\ \mathrm{M}_{\text{solute}}=\dfrac{0.52\times 10^{3}\times 2.5\times 10^{-3}}{75\times 10^{-3}\times 0.385} \\  \\ =45.02 \\  \\ \approx 45 \end{array}$

text:
For the reaction taking place in the cell :

$Pt (s)| H_{2} (g)|H^{+}(aq) || Ag^{+}(aq) |Ag (s)$

E${}_{cell}^{o}$ = + 0.5332 V.

The value of $\Delta_{f}$G${}^{\circ }$ is $______________ kJ$ mol$^{-1}. ($in nearest integer)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The cell reaction is $\mathrm{H}{}_{2}(\mathrm{g})+2\mathrm{Ag}{}^{+}(\mathrm{aq})\longrightarrow 2\mathrm{H}{}^{+}(\mathrm{aq})+2\mathrm{Ag}(\mathrm{s})$, with $n=2$.

$\Delta _{r}G^{\circ }=-nFE_{\text{cell}}^{\circ }=-2\times 96500\times 0.5332\text{J}=-102.9\text{kJ}$

Since $\Delta _{f}G^{\circ }$ of $\mathrm{H}{}_{2}(\mathrm{g})$, $\mathrm{Ag}(\mathrm{s})$ and $\mathrm{H}{}^{+}(\mathrm{aq})$ is zero, $\Delta _{r}G^{\circ }=-2\Delta _{f}G^{\circ }(\mathrm{Ag}{}^{+},\text{aq})$.

$\Delta _{f}G^{\circ }(\mathrm{Ag}{}^{+})=\dfrac{102.9}{2}\text{kJ mol}^{-1}=+51.45\text{kJ mol}^{-1}\approx 51\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$

Hence, the answer is 51.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th June Evening Shift

text:
It has been found that for a chemical reaction with rise in temperature by 9 K the rate constant gets doubled. Assuming a reaction to be occurring at 300 K, the value of activation energy is found to be $____________ kJ$ mol$^{-1}$. [nearest integer]

(Given $\ln 10 = 2.3, R = 8.3 J K^{-1}$ mol$^{-1}, \log  2 = 0.30)$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$T_{1}=300\mathrm{K}$

(Rate constant)

$\mathrm{K}_{2}=2\mathrm{K}_{1}$, on increase temperature by $9\mathrm{K}$

$\mathrm{T}_{2}=309\mathrm{K}$

$\mathrm{Ea}=?$

$\log \frac{\mathrm{K}_{2}}{\mathrm{K}_{1}}=\frac{\mathrm{Ea}}{2.3\mathrm{R}}\left [\frac{\mathrm{T}_{2}-\mathrm{T}_{1}}{\mathrm{T}_{2}\cdot \mathrm{T}_{1}}\right ]$

$\log 2=\frac{\mathrm{Ea}}{2.3\times 8.3}\left [\frac{9}{309\times 300}\right ]$

$\mathrm{Ea}=\frac{0.3\times 309\times 300\times 2.3\times 8.3}{9}$

$=58988.1\mathrm{J}/\mathrm{mole}$

$\simeq 59\mathrm{kJ}/\mathrm{mole}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th June Evening Shift

$=39.58$

$\simeq 40$
